headline: India’s ₹1.31 lakh crore railway project could break China’s record with world’s highest station in Ladakh | Details
content: India is planning a major railway infrastructure project in the Himalayas that could give the country the world's highest railway station, surpassing China's existing record. The proposed 489-km Bilaspur-Manali-Leh railway corridor is expected to feature a station at an altitude of approximately 5,256 metres (17,244 feet) above sea level.The proposed railway line will connect Bilaspur in Himachal Pradesh with Leh in Ladakh, bringing rail connectivity closer to India's northern frontier. With an estimated cost of ₹1.31 lakh crore, the project is among the country's most ambitious railway infrastructure proposals, The Times of India reported.According to project details, the Railway Ministry has completed the survey and prepared the Detailed Project Report (DPR). However, the project is yet to receive the necessary approval for construction.India's proposed railway station in Ladakh could surpass China's recordOne of the most significant features of the proposed railway corridor is a station planned beneath the Tanglang La mountain pass in Ladakh, according to a report by The Times of India.At an estimated elevation of 5,256 metres, the proposed station would be higher than China's Tanggula railway station on the Qinghai-Tibet Railway. Located at approximately 5,068 metres above sea level, the Chinese station is currently recognised as the world's highest railway station.If constructed as proposed, the Indian station would exceed China's record by nearly 188 metres.Tanglang La is already a challenging high-altitude location along the Manali-Leh highway. Establishing railway infrastructure in the region, however, would require significantly more complex engineering than constructing a motorable road.489-km Bilaspur-Manali-Leh railway line to have 270 km of tunnelsThe proposed Bilaspur-Manali-Leh railway corridor will cover approximately 489 km, connecting several important towns and settlements across Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh.The route is expected to pass through Bilaspur, Sundernagar, Mandi, Manali, Sissu, Darcha, Keylong, Sarchu, Pang, Rumtse, Upshi and Kharu before reaching Leh.A major engineering challenge will be the extensive tunnelling required to navigate the Himalayan mountain range. According to project details, approximately 270 km of the proposed railway line will pass through tunnels.This means that more than half of the corridor could run underground, highlighting the scale of engineering involved in the project.Construction would have to account for difficult geological formations, extreme weather conditions, steep mountain gradients and the challenges of working at high altitudes. These factors make the proposed railway corridor considerably more complex than conventional railway expansion projects.Why is India's proposed Ladakh railway project strategically important?The proposed railway line is not merely intended to improve passenger connectivity or reduce travel time to Ladakh. It also carries strategic significance for India's defence infrastructure.Leh and the surrounding areas are strategically important for the country. At present, connectivity to the region largely depends on road and air transport.The Manali-Leh highway serves as an important transportation route, but heavy snowfall and harsh weather conditions can disrupt movement, particularly during winter. Air connectivity offers another option, although it cannot provide the same transportation capacity as a large railway corridor for passengers and goods.A railway connection could offer an additional route for transporting essential supplies, equipment and passengers. It could also strengthen logistical connectivity to a strategically sensitive region.The Ministry of Defence's identification of the project as a strategic railway corridor underlines its significance beyond civilian transportation.When will the Bilaspur-Manali-Leh railway line be completed?Despite its ambitious scale, the proposed railway line remains at the planning stage.The Railway Ministry has completed the survey and prepared the Detailed Project Report, with the estimated project cost pegged at approximately ₹1.31 lakh crore. However, the preparation of a DPR does not automatically mean that construction has been approved.There is currently no confirmed completion deadline for the entire railway corridor.The project will require substantial financial investment, detailed engineering assessments and necessary clearances before construction can begin. Challenges involving other railway infrastructure projects in Himachal Pradesh could also influence the broader expansion of rail connectivity towards Ladakh.Land acquisition hurdles pose challenges for Himalayan railway expansionThe proposed Ladakh railway corridor is not the only major railway infrastructure project facing implementation challenges in Himachal Pradesh.The 63-km Bhanupali-Bilaspur-Beri railway line is another important project expected to strengthen rail connectivity in the state and support the broader expansion of the railway network towards Ladakh.However, the project has encountered delays related to land acquisition and the state's financial contribution.In October 2026, the Himachal Pradesh High Court quashed the preliminary land acquisition notification for the project. The court found that the government had not followed the statutory requirements for extending the deadline to issue the land acquisition declaration.For the proposed Bilaspur-Manali-Leh corridor, the implementation challenges could be considerably greater because of its longer route, extensive tunnelling requirements and difficult Himalayan geography.If the project receives the necessary approvals and is completed as proposed, it could significantly improve connectivity to Ladakh while potentially giving India a new entry in global railway history.

headline: Heat linked to 8,830 premature births in India; Uttar Pradesh, Bihar among worst-hit states: Study
content: The effects of extreme heat are reaching beyond the people exposed to soaring temperatures, with a new analysis estimating that human-caused climate change contributed to 8,830 premature births in India during the exceptionally hot April of 2024. The burden was concentrated in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Jharkhand, which together accounted for nearly two-thirds of the additional preterm births recorded in the country during the month.The findings, published by Zero Carbon Analytics (ZCA) on November 2, highlight how rising temperatures are becoming a maternal and newborn health concern, rather than remaining limited to environmental and weather-related risks.The analysis estimates that the April 2024 heat event was associated with around 16,150 additional preterm births across India, Bangladesh and the Philippines compared with a typical April. Of these, approximately 10,600 were specifically attributed to the additional warming caused by human activity.India accounted for 10,050 of the additional births associated with the heat event, representing a 3.6 per cent increase over the usual April level. The corresponding increase was 11.9 per cent in Bangladesh and 10 per cent in the Philippines.The study also found that human-induced climate change had made the April 2024 heat event in South Asia around 45 times more likely. The impact was not evenly distributed across India. While West Bengal recorded a 10 per cent rise in preterm birth risk and Bihar 7 per cent, Uttar Pradesh saw a rise of around 3 per cent. Its high number of additional cases was largely linked to its population size.The implications could become more serious as temperatures continue to rise. Using future climate projections, researchers estimate that India could record around 15,300 additional preterm births during a typical April by mid-century, between 2041 and 2060. Uttar Pradesh is projected to face the highest burden, followed by Bihar and Rajasthan. Bangladesh could see around 1,500 additional cases during an ordinary April over the same period.Premature births, defined as deliveries before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy, are a leading cause of newborn deaths worldwide. Babies born early can face serious health complications, including problems affecting their physical and neurological development.Dr Rashmi Agarwalla, Associate Professor in the Department of Community and Family Medicine at AIIMS Guwahati and its climate change nodal officer, has highlighted how anaemia, poor nutrition and prolonged outdoor work can increase heat-related risks for pregnant women, particularly in vulnerable communities.The analysis also points to gaps in maternal healthcare preparedness. Although India has issued pregnancy-specific heat guidance and several state heat action plans recognise pregnant women as vulnerable, protection measures are not yet consistently integrated into routine maternal care.Improved antenatal care, access to cooling facilities and early warning systems could reduce some of these risks. However, the researchers stress that these measures alone cannot address the growing burden without limiting global warming.

headline: Recruitment for more than 11,000 posts in Bihar’s health department to begin soon
content: PATNA Bihar’s Health department is all set to begin the process to fill more than 11,000 administrative, technical and medical support positions. Sharing the information, State Health Society Executive Director Nawal Kishore Chaudhary on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) said the official recruitment notification for this massive hiring drive is expected to be issued by the last week of this month. Preparations for the recruitment process are almost complete, he said adding that a recruitment calendar will also be released shortly. Currently, updated details of vacant positions have been sought from all 38 districts of the State. The information is being gathered from district-level health institutions, Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centres (CHCs) and Sub-Divisional Hospitals. According to the Executive Director, recruitment will be carried out for several positions, including Staff Nurses, Laboratory Technicians, managerial-category posts, Block Health Managers (BHM), NME personnel at the block level, and clerical staff. The recruitment for several other vacant positions will be undertaken in the second phase. Mr. Chaudhary, added that the completion of the first phase of recruitment for more than 11,000 posts will undoubtedly bring significant and positive changes to Bihar’s healthcare sector. “Dedicated teams will be made available at the block and panchayat levels to support doctors and paramedical staff, thereby improving the quality of primary healthcare services in remote areas especially in rural areas. The number of healthcare workers in district and sub-divisional hospitals will be better aligned with patient loads, reducing the excessive workload on existing employees, “Mr. Chaudhary said. He pointed out that an adequate number of laboratory technicians and nurses will ensure that patients receive timely diagnostic reports and quality healthcare services. He mentioned that the appointment of Block Health Managers and clerical staff will also help ensure that government healthcare schemes reach the general public more efficiently and in, transparent and quick manner. Mr. Chaudhary further stated that the recruitment calendar has almost been finalised and will be made public as soon as it gets approval from the authorities concerned. The department’s primary objective is to complete the entire recruitment process- including selection, document verification and distribution of appointment letters- in a transparent manner within 6 to 7 months from the date of the issuance of the official notification, he added.

headline: NACIN ZTI Kolkata Signs MoU with Government of Sikkim to Strengthen GST Administration
content: The National Academy of Customs, Indirect Taxes and Narcotics (NACIN), Zonal Training Institute (ZTI), Kolkata, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Commercial Taxes Division (CTD), Finance Department, Government of Sikkim, at Gangtok on November 2, 2026. The collaboration aims to strengthen the State’s Goods and Services Tax (GST) administration through professional training, capacity building and continuous knowledge sharing. The MoU was signed by Principal Additional Director General, NACIN ZTI Kolkata, Shri Atul Saxena on behalf of the institute, and Secretary-cum-Commissioner, Commercial Taxes Division, Shri Manoj Rai on behalf of the Government of Sikkim. Officers from NACIN Kolkata, the CGST office in Sikkim and CTD Sikkim attended the programme, along with representatives of trade bodies and tax consultants. The MoU envisages a structured framework for professional training and capacity building between NACIN ZTI Kolkata and the Commercial Taxes Division, Sikkim. The partnership is intended to equip tax officers with updated knowledge, enhanced technical competencies and practical insights to address the evolving requirements of GST administration. NACIN Kolkata will henceforth, work with the State authorities to develop customised training programmes for Sikkim SGST officers, taking into account the State’s administrative and economic requirements. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rai emphasised the importance of continuous academic support and specialised training for tax officers in view of evolving tax laws and frequent reforms. He stated that the MoU would provide a platform for formal training, skill development, academic interaction and knowledge sharing with officers of NACIN Kolkata, as well as officers of West Bengal SGST and CGST. Shri Saxena highlighted NACIN’s role in providing professional training to officers dealing with Customs, Indirect Taxes and Narcotics across the country. He appreciated the initiative taken by the Government of Sikkim and noted the significant developments in the GST ecosystem since its introduction on July 1, 2017.

headline: From online barbs to street mobilisation: How BJP is reshaping its communication strategy
content: New Delhi: From sharp social media attacks and political songs targeting opposition leaders to marches, rallies and public meetings across states, the BJP is increasingly combining its digital outreach with street-level mobilisation to amplify its political messaging and counter the opposition's narrative. .The party's ongoing 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) campaign reflects this evolving approach, with its leaders and workers taking the political contest beyond online platforms and carrying the party's message to streets, public spaces and university campuses. .The renewed push follows the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, where opposition leaders accused the BJP of electoral irregularities and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. .Rahul Gandhi’s new protest playbook redefines grammar of dissent.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also warned that the CEC would face action in the future for alleged electoral wrongdoing. .The BJP responded by stepping up its counter-offensive, accusing the opposition of undermining democratic institutions and questioning the Election Commission's credibility. .Its campaign has been marked by coordinated programmes across states, with its senior leaders, Union ministers and state functionaries taking part in marches, public meetings and press conferences. .“The entire campaign, from padayatras to online and digital outreach programmes, is being run in coordination with the state units. One of the main focus areas is exposing Rahul Gandhi's lies by presenting facts before the people, including on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls,” a BJP source told PTI. .EC-SIR protests | Why the BJP, born of protest politics, is struggling to handle dissent.“Our teams are working across districts, telling the youth about the falsehoods being spread by Rahul Gandhi, not just in BJP-ruled states but also those ruled by the opposition. .“People are being told how Rahul Gandhi is working with foreign forces to destabilise the country. A major focus of this campaign is to tell the people that Rahul Gandhi is only interested in a regime change with foreign help,” the source added. .BJP president Nitin Nabin is leading the party's organisational push, with marches planned in different parts of the country. .Union ministers Amit Shah, J P Nadda and Shivraj Singh Chouhan, among others, are also participating in the programmes, while state leaders have been tasked with mobilising party workers and taking the campaign to the grassroots. .The party is also using social media to sharpen its attacks on the opposition leaders, particularly Rahul Gandhi, through videos, songs, graphics and pointed political messages. .The digital campaigns have become a prominent feature of its efforts to frame the political debate and counter the allegations levelled by the opposition parties. .What makes the latest campaign significant is the way the BJP is attempting to connect its online messaging with physical mobilisation. .While social media allows the party to circulate its political narrative rapidly and reach a wider audience, marches and public meetings provide an opportunity to translate that messaging into visible political action. .The involvement of student organisations has added another dimension to this outreach. .The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), the student wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), is organising rallies and protest marches, including a mega student rally at Delhi University, taking the campaign to educational institutions and mobilising the youth around the party's political narrative. .ABVP national general secretary Virendra Singh Solanki said that through the 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' campaign and student rallies, the organisation is raising a strong voice against the attempts by Rahul Gandhi and the opposition to create distrust in democratic institutions and undermine democratic values. .He said the success of ABVP's rallies in major educational centres, including in Lucknow, Patna, Delhi and Himachal Pradesh, reflects the growing support among students for democratic values and constructive leadership. .“Rahul Gandhi may try to project himself as the voice of Gen-Z, but he does not represent the aspirations of India's youth. Instead, such attempts seek to mislead young people. The response to ABVP's nationwide campaign clearly reflects that students are rejecting this narrative and voluntarily coming forward to associate themselves with the ABVP," he claimed. .BJP's strategy also underlines the importance of its extensive organisational network, which allows national political messaging to be carried forward by state units, local leaders and affiliated bodies. .By holding parallel programmes, the party is seeking to maintain a sustained political presence rather than limiting its response to statements by senior leaders or social media exchanges. .The growing convergence of digital campaigns and street politics reflects a broader change in political communication, where parties are increasingly using online platforms not as a substitute for traditional mobilisation, but as a means to reinforce it. .For the BJP, the challenge lies in ensuring that the visibility generated by online campaigns translates into wider public engagement and sustained political support. .As the contest with the opposition intensifies, the party's latest campaign reflects how political messaging is increasingly being fought simultaneously on digital platforms and on the streets. .Anup Sharma, a political communications consultant, said the BJP has always been ahead of the curve when it came to political outreach; it recognised the power of social media early, built an extensive WhatsApp network and used digital platforms to shape electoral narratives. .“However, the Gen Z protests have triggered a rethink. What is interesting is that the BJP is not abandoning its established strengths but recalibrating its approach. .“Greater emphasis on social listening, sentiment analysis, data intelligence and analytical tools is becoming central to understanding voter behaviour, emerging discontent and constituency-level issues,” Sharma said. .Equally, the party knows that digital engagement alone cannot win elections and therefore it continues to combine social media campaigns with rallies, padayatras, local outreach and its extensive grassroots organisation, he said. .“The BJP's challenge today is not simply to dominate social media, as it once did, but to stay ahead of changing voter behaviour. Winning the algorithm may get attention, but understanding voter sentiment is what builds political connect,” Sharma added.

headline: Keralam BJP asks Rahul Gandhi to go to Bangladesh, accuses him of 'creating anarchy'
content: In the wake of protests by Congress-led Opposition parties against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Keralam BJP president Rajeev Chandrasekhar on Thursday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of "attempting to create anarchy" in India. ."If Rahul Gandhi wants to create anarchy, let him go to Bangladesh. Let him do his politics there, with the Jamaat-e-Islami that backs him," Chandrasekhar said in a social media post. .He said Gandhi's "dream" would never materialise in India, asserting that the country's democracy was protected by the BJP and 140 crore Indians. .The Nemom MLA and former Union Minister of State said the Congress had lost the elections in 2014 and 2019 and was defeated again in 2024 despite allegedly resorting to false propaganda. .Rahul advocating regime change on lines of Bangladesh; seeking foreign intervention: Pralhad Joshi.Chandrasekhar said the message given by the people had been clearly understood by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha. .He alleged that the Congress could no longer win the confidence of the people and that voters would not support the party based on its governance in Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana and Keralam. .He further alleged that Gandhi was attempting to divert public attention by spreading falsehoods and creating anarchy in the country to defeat Prime Minister Narendra Modi. With PTI inputs

headline: EC announces Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in six states & UTs; final list to be published on Jan 21
content: New Delhi: The Election Commission has announced a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in six more states and union territories – Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim – where the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) was completed in the third phase. The fresh exercise seeks to enroll eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors, and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1 and October 1, 2027. The draft voter list will be published on November 30 while the final rolls will be published on January 21 next year, according to letters sent to the Chief Electoral Officers of the six states and UTs on Wednesday. .Pilibhit voters' list controversy: Election Commission orders suspension of two EROs.The rationalisation or rearrangement of polling stations should be completed by November 20. The period for filing claims and objections would start from November 30 and end on December 30 and it would be disposed of by January 16. Chief Secretaries have been instructed to ensure adequate manpower and resources for the exercise. The SSR exercise has not been announced in ten states and UTs, including Karnataka, where SIR is underway or has just been completed. The schedule for SSR in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh where SIR has not been started so far will also be announced later. Earlier on October 15, the EC had announced the SSR exercise in 17 states and union territories where the SIR was completed in the first two phases. The process has already started in these states with the rationalisation of polling booths was finalised on November 2. The draft rolls are scheduled for November 12 and the final rolls on January 4 next year. .'Political change in democracy can come only through elections': RSS justifies SIR, warns against 'anarchist forces'.The delay in conducting the SSR in states where the contentious SIR was finished was a bone of contention in the poll body with Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raising concerns. The delay also led to claims that voters turning 18 were finding it difficult to register as voters. One of the notable changes in the latest SSR is the decision to provide parties with “soft copy of draft and final rolls in readable PDF format without photos of the electors” free of cost along with a physical copy. For candidates, a readable PDF of alphabetically arranged electoral rolls in pen drive or any other electronic storage device will be provided on payment at the time of polls. The EC had earlier refused to provide machine readable electoral rolls, a demand continuously raised by the Opposition, including top Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, to enable them to compare it with previous voter lists to locate anomalies. The poll body had earlier argued that providing such rolls would compromise the integrity of the voter list and could be manipulated.

headline: Poll-bound states have higher representation in India's defence forces
content: Data available on state-wise representation of defence personnel bears out that youth from Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Manipur join the armed forces in significant numbers. This comes as the Opposition, including the Congress, linked overhauling the Agnipath scheme to the upcoming elections in five states. Assembly elections are slated to be held in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur around February-March 2027. On Wednesday, Congress Rajya Sabha member and spokesperson Pawan Khera termed the decision as another “flip” by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). “With elections approaching in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Manipur and Himachal Pradesh — states with high per capita recruitment rates in the Indian Armed Forces — the government has announced a major change to the Agniveer scheme,” Khera said. After Agniveer was announced, besides the Congress, BJP’s allies also flagged their concerns on the scheme after the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. In the Lok Sabha polls, the BJP bagged 240 seats, falling short of the majority mark by 32 seats, and relied on its allies to form the government. In one of their first demands at the time, allies, such as the Janata Dal (United), Telugu Desam Party and Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) demanded a review of the Agnipath scheme. These parties spoke of the resentment against the scheme among youths. Widespread protests had taken place in Bihar, UP, Rajasthan and parts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana when the scheme was announced in 2022. According to the government’s reply in the Rajya Sabha in July 2022, train services were affected due to agitation and protests against the Agnipath scheme at 62 locations. A total of 2,132 trains were cancelled between June 15 and June 22. A total refund of nearly ₹102.96 crore was given because of train cancellations and “a loss of ₹259.44 crore due to damage and destruction of railway assets in agitations against Agnipath scheme was incurred.” The state-wise data of recruitment under the Agnipath scheme is unavailable. But there is data available on the state-wise recruitment in the defence forces. The Department of Military Affairs, which comes under the Ministry of Defence, furnished the data in a reply in the Lok Sabha on April 1, 2022. According to the data, there were 1,133,083 (around 1.13 million) personnel of junior commissioned officers (JCOs) and other ranks as on December 31, 2021 in the Indian Army. Of these, 22,880 were from Nepal and 14 from Bhutan. JCOs and other ranks recruited from Indian states and Union Territories comprised 1,110,079 (around 1.11 million). Among these, Uttar Pradesh had the maximum representation of 162,724, or 14.65 per cent. Punjab’s share was 90,290, or 8.13 per cent, Uttarakhand’s 59,978 or 5.4 per cent and Manipur’s 8,565, or less than one per cent. Goa’s representation was 219, including 15 JCOs and the rest of other ranks. UP and Punjab were the top two states in terms of representation of JCOs and other ranks in the Indian Army, followed by Maharashtra (84,373) and Rajasthan (80,034). Uttarakhand, along with Bihar and Haryana, was also among the top states in terms of representation of JCOs and other ranks in the Indian Army. In the Indian Navy, of its 10,169 officers, there were 1,486 from UP, the highest for any state. While coastal states, such as Kerala (1,033), Maharashtra (745), Andhra Pradesh (601) and Tamil Nadu (579) led in the representation in the Indian Navy’s officer ranks, Uttarakhand (413) and Punjab (381) also had a significant presence. And, 56 were from Manipur and 35 from Goa, Daman and Diu. Among Indian Navy’s 63,700 sailors, those from UP were the highest at 11,946, followed by Rajasthan (8,202), Haryana (6,237), Bihar (5,964), Andhra Pradesh (3,677), Madhya Pradesh (3,043), Maharashtra (2,854), and Kerala (2,542). There were 1,578 sailors from Uttarakhand and 1,464 from Punjab, 459 from Manipur and 92 from Goa. Among the Indian Air Force’s 12,143 officers, 2,134 were from UP, 1,137 from Haryana, 824 from Maharashtra, 749 from Kerala, 729 from Delhi, 664 from Punjab, 632 from Uttarakhand, 63 from Manipur and 29 from Goa. Of the 138,994 Airmen in the Indian Air Force, those from UP were the highest at 35,942, followed by Bihar (21,931), Haryana (16,024), and Rajasthan (15,868). There were 5,425 airmen from Uttarakhand, 1,924 from Punjab, 1,417 from Manipur and 43 from Goa. The big pictureArmy: Uttar Pradesh (UP) leads with 14.65% of JCOs and other ranks, followed by Punjab (8.13%) and Uttarakhand (5.4%)Navy officers: UP tops the list with 1,486 personnel; Uttarakhand has 413 and Punjab 381Navy sailors: UP leads with 11,946, followed by Uttarakhand (1,578) and Punjab (1,464)Air force officers: UP has 2,134 personnel, followed by Punjab (664) and Uttarakhand (632)Airmen: UP leads with 35,942, while Uttarakhand has 5,425 and Punjab 1,924

headline: Himachal to introduce Rs 10 lakh health insurance scheme, eight companies participate in tender: Naresh Chauhan
content: Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 5 (ANI): Himachal Pradesh government is preparing to introduce a new health insurance scheme offering coverage of up to Rs 10 lakh per family, replacing the existing Rs 5-lakh Himcare scheme, Principal Media Advisor to Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Naresh Chauhan, said on Thursday.Speaking to ANI in Shimla, Chauhan said eight insurance companies had participated in the tendering process for the proposed scheme, with Birla Sun Life emerging as the lowest bidder. He said Chief Minister Sukhu had directed the Health Secretary to hold further negotiations with the company to finalise the process and expedite the implementation of the scheme.Chauhan said the new model had been designed after the state government received complaints of alleged corruption and misuse of funds under the Himcare scheme. Preliminary inquiries had reportedly pointed towards a nexus involving certain private hospitals and nursing homes, including facilities outside Himachal Pradesh, leading to alleged irregularities in medical claims.He said the government intended to ensure greater transparency and strengthen healthcare delivery, particularly for families unable to afford expensive medical treatment."People living below the poverty line and those covered under other eligible welfare schemes will certainly benefit from the proposed scheme. Its coverage will be enhanced from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh per family, while the scope of beneficiaries will also be expanded," Chauhan said.He added that the proposed insurance-based model would help curb irregularities and ensure that public money was utilised effectively. The government was also working to strengthen the healthcare infrastructure through advanced medical technology, robotic surgery, PET-CT scan facilities, MRI and X-ray machines, besides recruitment of doctors and other healthcare staff.On the Union government's recent decision concerning the Agnipath recruitment scheme, Chauhan said Congress had opposed the policy from its inception, arguing that four years of service were insufficient for young people aspiring to build careers in the armed forces."Recruiting young people into the armed forces for just four years raises serious questions about their future and the future of the military. Even extending the tenure by two years does not adequately address the issue. There should be a minimum service period of 10 years, preferably 15 years," he said.He added that the Congress and the INDIA bloc would bring changes to the Agnipath scheme if they came to power at the Centre.On the disciplinary action against more than 200 Youth Congress office-bearers across seven states, Chauhan said the action had been taken against those who failed to participate in the recent protest movement.He said participation in the movement was mandatory for office-bearers of both the Youth Congress and Congress."Those who did not participate in the movement have faced action. The All India Youth Congress will take a further decision on the matter," he said.Commenting on Congress's campaign against alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Chauhan said the issue of electoral transparency had emerged as a major concern across the country.He said Rahul Gandhi had repeatedly raised questions over the fairness of elections during the past three years, alleging that electoral processes were being influenced through deletion of voters' names, addition of voters and the use of government resources to influence the electorate."Democracy is the country's greatest strength. Governments will come and go, but democracy and the Constitution must remain strong. The struggle is aimed at ensuring transparency in the electoral process and protecting democratic institutions," he said.Referring to the recent US midterm election results, Chauhan said they demonstrated that voters ultimately had the power to hold governments accountable, irrespective of how powerful those in authority might be.He said the message was equally relevant for India, where democratic institutions and electoral transparency needed to be protected.On the proposed health insurance scheme, Chauhan said the government was working to finalise the tendering process and the premium structure, adding that further details would be announced after negotiations with the selected insurance company. (ANI)

headline: CM Sukhu announces ₹3 crore for science lab at Chamba School, 8 additional classrooms
content: Announcement follows student’s request for better science education facilities during CM’s interaction at Tissa school Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu has announced ₹3 crore for the construction of a science laboratory and eight additional classrooms at Government Model Senior Secondary School in Tissa, Chamba district. The announcement came during the Chief Minister’s interaction with students, when a science student, Ishika Bhardwaj, highlighted the lack of a modern laboratory and essential equipment at the school. She stressed the need for better laboratory facilities to make science education more effective. Taking the student's concern seriously, Sukhu immediately announced ₹3 crore for the science lab along with the construction of eight additional classrooms. The Chief Minister received a warm welcome from students, who greeted him with applause and enthusiasm. Instead of limiting his visit to a formal program, he sat among the students, listened to their concerns and responded to questions related to education, career prospects, the education system and social issues. The proposed infrastructure upgrades are expected to provide students with better learning facilities and an improved academic environment.

headline: Himachal CM Sukhu announces Rs 3 crore for school lab, classrooms in Chamba
content: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Thursday announced a grant of Rs 3 crore for the construction of a school laboratory and additional classrooms at Bairagarh School, while asserting that the state government was taking strict action against drug mafias and would not spare those involved in the illegal drug trade. Sukhu made the announcement while interacting with students of PM SHRI [https://news.careers360.com/centre-asks-keralam-decide-on-pm-shri-scheme-at-earliest] Government Model Senior Secondary School, Tissa, in Chamba district, before flagging off an Anti-Chitta (adulterated heroin) walkathon to raise awareness about drug abuse. The chief minister said the government was also confiscating properties of people involved in drug trafficking and asserted that there was no place for those engaged in the illegal drug trade in the state. He said the fight against drugs was not merely the responsibility of the government but a shared responsibility of every section of society. ANTI-CHITTA WALKATHON Anti-chitta rallies and awareness programmes were being organised across the state to educate young people and the general public about the harmful effects of chitta and other intoxicating substances and encourage them to stay away from drugs, according to a statement issued here. Also read Share teachers before school closure; mergers, student relocation must be last resort: EAC PM paper [https://news.careers360.com/eac-pm-paper-on-schools-closure-merger-last-resort-nep-teacher-sharing-student-enrollment-dropout-anganwadi-udise-plus-travel-cost] Sukhu said young people had a particularly important role to play in spreading awareness against drug abuse. A large number of students participated in the walkathon, carrying the message of public awareness against drugs. He appealed to people to inform the police about drug traffickers by calling the emergency helpline number 112. He assured them that the identity of anyone providing such information would be kept completely confidential. Earlier, the chief minister encouraged students of the school to work hard and strive for success in life. Responding to a question from Tamanna, a Class 12 student, he said students should make decisions fearlessly to move forward and achieve their goals. During the interaction, Monika, another Class 12 student, asked about the steps being taken by the government to prevent drug abuse, while Muskan sought information about measures to improve the quality of education and facilities in government schools. Sukhu said challenges would arise at every stage of life, but those who made the right decisions at the right time without fear were the ones who created history. Responding to the students' demands, Sukhu announced a grant of Rs 3 crore for the construction of a school laboratory and additional classrooms at Bairagarh School.

headline: Una leads in Himachal Pradesh with over 110 tobacco-free villages | Hindustan Times
content: Una, With 112 villages declared tobacco-free, Una district has secured the top position in Himachal Pradesh under the third phase of the 'Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign' , according to officials.Building on this achievement, the district administration has intensified efforts to bring the remaining villages into the fold, aiming for a 100 per cent success rate.According to official sources, there are about 868 villages in Una district.Commending the efforts of the Health Department, block medical officers , and block development officers , Deputy Commissioner Jatin Lal on Thursday instructed all relevant departments to work in close coordination during the fourth phase of the campaign.He said that the fourth phase of the Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign , which commenced on October 28, will continue until December 26.During this period, all departments are expected to work collectively to curb tobacco consumption, raise awareness among the youth regarding its harmful effects, and ensure compliance with tobacco control regulations.The deputy commissioner directed that special Gram Sabhas be organised at the panchayat level and emphasised that these meetings should focus on educating the public about the adverse effects of tobacco products and other intoxicating substances, including chitta .Panchayat representatives should be briefed on their roles and the authority vested in them regarding tobacco control, enabling them to play an active part in advancing this initiative within their respective villages.DC Lal directed sub-divisional magistrates , deputy superintendents of police and the concerned BMOs to visit colleges and conduct awareness sessions for students.He stressed the importance of educating the youth about the harmful effects of tobacco and narcotics, and encouraging them to abstain from their use.Furthermore, the officer issued instructions to ensure compliance with established standards for 'tobacco-free' campuses, conduct regular awareness activities, and enforce the ban on the sale of tobacco products within a 100-yard radius of educational institutions.He also directed all heads of departments to ensure that their offices and workplaces remain tobacco-free. Urban local bodies were instructed to review the licenses and stipulated conditions for vendors selling tobacco products within their respective jurisdictions.The deputy commissioner tasked all relevant departments, including the Police, Excise and Taxation, Food Safety, and Health departments, with conducting regular inspections based on their respective mandates and taking appropriate legal action in cases of violations.Action will be taken under the provisions of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act , 2003; the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act , 2019; the Himachal Pradesh Tobacco Control Act, 2016; and the Food Safety and Standards Regulations.Enforcement teams have been directed to ensure a ban on the sale of loose cigarettes and bidis and to take action against gutkha or khaini and similar products through food safety officials.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Sale of Electricity to Rajasthan to Generate ₹400 Crore Revenue for Himachal in Four Months: CM Sukhu
content: Churah/Chamba – Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu has said that the state government expects to generate revenue of around ₹400 crore over the next four months through the sale of electricity to Rajasthan at the rate of ₹15.50 per unit. Describing the agreement as a significant step towards strengthening the state’s financial position, the Chief Minister said the government had taken concrete measures to improve Himachal Pradesh’s economy and move towards self-reliance. He said that under the agreement, electricity would be supplied to Rajasthan at a rate of ₹15.50 per unit, which is expected to generate approximately ₹400 crore in additional revenue for the state during the next four months. The Chief Minister said his government was committed to making Himachal Pradesh economically self-reliant by strengthening revenue sources and plugging all avenues of corruption. He emphasised that the government was taking important decisions to ensure better utilisation of the state’s available resources and improve its financial position. Sukhu also highlighted the state’s efforts to secure a larger share of free power from hydroelectric projects. He said the state government had strongly taken up the matter with the Central Government to increase Himachal Pradesh’s free power share in the 180 MW Baira-Siul Hydroelectric Project to 50 per cent. He said the demand had been raised following the completion of 44 years of the project’s operation, stressing that Himachal Pradesh should receive a fairer share of benefits from hydropower projects located in the state.

headline: Chandigarh University Ranks No. 1 Among Private Universities in India for the 4th Year in a Row in QS Asia University Rankings 2027
content: PRNewswireChandigarh [India], November 4: Maintaining its position as the top-most university, Chandigarh University has yet again emerged as India's Number 1 Private University in India for the fourth consecutive year in the latest edition of prestigious QS Asia University Rankings 2027. Earlier, Chandigarh University had secured the 1st rank among all private universities in India in 2024, 2025 and 2026 editions of the QS Asia University Rankings.Chandigarh University continued its stellar rise among top universities in Asia also by rising 4 places to achieve the 104th rank among all Asian universities in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027 published by the London-based university ranking organization QS, by improving its overall score from 66.6 in 2026 to 70.3 in 2027's rankings. Chandigarh University has significantly improved its position in the QS Asia University Rankings, rising from 271st in 2022 to 104th place in 2027, reflecting an impressive improvement of 61% over the past six years on the basis of its robust performance on most indicators.With this, Chandigarh University has leapfrogged to secure better ranks than many international universities in top Asian countries including China, Japan, South Korea among others.Overall, Chandigarh University improved its score for most performance indicators. While Chandigarh University climbed 59 ranks in International Research Network (IRN) to secure 35th rank among top universities in Asia, it also rose four places to secure 48th rank in Employer Reputation, strengthening its standing among Asia's leading universities in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027.Welcoming India's remarkable performance in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and Chandigarh University Chancellor Satnam Singh Sandhu said, "Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Indian higher educational institutions (HEIs) have made impressive strides, both globally and within Asia, as evidenced by the QS Asia University Rankings 2027. The fact that 325 institutions including 31 new entrants from India made it to the QS Asia Rankings 2027 shows the new National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 has led to qualitative changes in India's education sector. With the Union government further boosting research and innovation, India has well established itself as a formidable competitor among global education powerhouses. With the unprecedented rise in QS Asia University Rankings, more and more Indian institutions than ever before are earning their place on the world stage. India has solidified its reputation as an emerging hub for higher learning in Asia with reforms promoting quality, research, innovation, and international collaboration. While IIT Delhi leads the Indian contingent, the spectacular rise of young institutions like Chandigarh University in short span of time shows the growth and resilience of India's educational landscape in the past 12 years. It shows India's commitment to fostering academic excellence and enhancing global competitiveness of its education institutions at the global level."Commenting on Chandigarh University's remarkable rise in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027, Chandigarh University Vice Chancellor Prof (Dr) SS Sehgal said, "It indeed is a proud moment that Chandigarh University has become the first private university to secure the number 1 rank for the fourth consecutive year. Chandigarh University has been recognised as one of the top universities in Asia and improved 4 places to achieve 104th place among higher educational institutions in the largest continent in the world which indeed is a marvellous feat. As a research-intensive university, Chandigarh University has an impressive 6,712 patents and 29,824 research publications to its credit. In past one year, Chandigarh University has filed over 964 patents, 824 of its patents have been published and 55 patents have been granted. This apart, over 7,578 research papers of Chandigarh University have been published in a year. This is the reason Chandigarh University has secured the 35th rank in Asia in the International Research Network (IRN). Likewise, in Employer Reputation indicator - which measures how institutions and their programmes are perceived by employers involved in graduate recruitment and hiring decisions -- Chandigarh University ranks among Asia's top 50 universities. This is the reason over 1,300 top MNCs come to CU campus for placements and made over 10,000 job offers to CU students during Campus Placement drive in previous academic year.""Chandigarh University's remarkable performance in the latest QS Asia University Rankings is testament to our unwavering commitment to provide academic excellence and world class education to our students. Rankings such as these are not just about numbers; they reflect the collective effort of our faculty, staff, and students. Being number 1 private university, we remain dedicated to continuous improvement and innovation, driving forward with the same passion and determination that has brought us this far," Prof Sehgal added.About Chandigarh UniversityChandigarh University is a NAAC A+ Grade University and QS World Ranked University. This autonomous educational institution is approved by UGC and is located near Chandigarh in the state of Punjab. It is the youngest university in India and the only private university in Punjab to be honoured with A+ Grade by NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council). CU offers more than 109 UG and PG programs in the field of engineering, management, pharmacy, law, architecture, journalism, animation, hotel management, commerce, and others. It has been awarded as The University with Best Placements by WCRC.Website address: https://www.cuchd.in/(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by PRNewswire. ANI will not be responsible in any way for the content of the same.)

headline: US sanctions Indian businessman, wife for helping Iran evade oil curbs
content: The United States has imposed sanctions on an India-based businessman, his wife and several associated companies over allegations that they helped Iran evade international restrictions on its oil trade through fraudulent maritime registrations. In a press release on Wednesday (local time), the US Department of the Treasury said the action was part of US President Donald Trump's Operation Economic Outcast, a campaign aimed at cutting off Iran's oil revenues and restricting its ability to finance its war with the US. Who are the Indians targeted by the US? The US Treasury said the sanctions targeted what it described as a 'vast criminal network' operated by Chandigarh-based businessman Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid. The network allegedly supported Iran's shadow fleet through maritime fraud by providing false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum. Some of these vessels were allegedly operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies. The action also covers two other Indian nationals, Ashwani Kumar Dhiman and Ishwinder Singh, who are accused of heading two businesses connected to the couple. Nine India-linked entities associated with Sharma have also been named in the sanctions. Sharma's network allegedly claimed to provide flagging services on behalf of several countries and territories, including Aruba, Guyana, Mali, Mozambique, Malawi, Sint Maarten and Timor-Leste. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned individuals and businesses against supporting Tehran. "As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us," Bessent said. "We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime, whether by land, sea, or air." What do the US sanctions mean for the Indian entities? Under the sanctions, the property and financial interests of the designated individuals and companies that fall within US jurisdiction will be frozen. US citizens and businesses are generally prohibited from conducting transactions with them unless authorised by the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). The restrictions can also extend to other companies that are at least 50 per cent owned, directly or indirectly, by sanctioned individuals or entities. The Treasury said non-US individuals and businesses could also face consequences for facilitating transactions that violate US sanctions or helping others evade them. Which other countries and entities have the US sanctioned? Separately, Washington has targeted Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services, accusing it of providing ground-handling and other services to six US-sanctioned Iranian airlines. These include Iran Air Tour, Saha Airlines, Sepehran Airlines, Varesh Airlines, Taban Airlines and Ata Airlines Company. The US said the wider network helped Iran's shadow fleet transport oil while concealing the vessels' identities and ownership through fraudulent maritime documentation. Some of the ships allegedly operated on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies.

headline: Agriversity Organises Consultation Workshop on Natural Farming
content: Palampur, November 5, 2026: Chaudhary Sarwan Kumar Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya (CSKHPKV), Palampur, through its Directorate of Extension Education, organised a One-Day Consultation Workshop on Natural Farming on November 5, 2026, on the theme “Expert Perspectives, Practitioners’ Experiences and Emerging Entrepreneurship Opportunities.” The workshop brought together around 150 participants, including agricultural scientists, subject experts, extension professionals, Programme Coordinators, Nodal Officers from all Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) across Zone-I, and natural farming entrepreneurs, for deliberations on the scientific foundations, practical challenges and emerging entrepreneurial opportunities in natural farming. The inaugural session was attended by Dr. Pardeep Kumar, Dean Academics, Central University of Himachal Pradesh, Dharamshala, as the Chief Guest; Dr. Parvender Sheoran, Director, ICAR-ATARI, Ludhiana, as the Guest of Honour; and Dr. Atul Dogra, State Nodal Officer (SPNF) and Additional Director Agriculture, Shimla, as the Special Guest. Dr. Janardan Singh, Director of Extension Education, CSKHPKV, welcomed the participants, while Dr. Rajesh Kumar Rana, Nodal Officer (Natural Farming), ICAR-ATARI, Ludhiana, provided the background and context for the deliberations. The scientific session, themed “Scientific and Institutional Perspectives on Natural Farming in Relation to Entrepreneurship Opportunities,” featured detailed discussions by experts from agricultural research and extension institutions. The deliberations focused on the scientific assessment of natural farming practices, their effectiveness under different agro-climatic conditions, institutional support mechanisms and the need for evidence-based recommendations to strengthen the natural farming ecosystem. A major highlight of the workshop was the interactive session on “Practitioners’ Experiences and Innovations on Entrepreneurship Development in Natural Farming.” Natural farming entrepreneurs shared their first-hand experiences, innovations and practical challenges encountered during field implementation. The session facilitated a meaningful two-way exchange, with practitioners presenting their concerns, observations and suggestions, while scientists and experts offered technical insights and scientific perspectives. The interaction brought field realities into the scientific discourse and identified areas requiring further research, validation and extension support. The discussions underscored the importance of scientific validation, location-specific technologies, systematic documentation of practitioners’ experiences, effective extension support and stronger market linkages. Participants emphasised that addressing field-level constraints through research-based interventions is essential to making natural farming technically feasible, economically viable and sustainable. During the valedictory session, Dr. Pankaj Sood, Programme Coordinator, KVK Mandi, presented the key recommendations and way forward. Dr. Parvender Sheoran, Director, ICAR-ATARI, Ludhiana, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest, while Dr. Janardan Singh, Director of Extension Education, CSKHPKV, was the Guest of Honour. Dr. Sonia Sood, Associate Director Extension Education, proposed the vote of thanks and expressed gratitude to the dignitaries, scientists and participating entrepreneurs.
